speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person vandana)
question: What is the object of veneration, and how does veneration relate to it?
premises: The object is fixed in full: all-pervading (vyāpta) particular of moving-and-unmoving states (carācarabhāvaviśeṣa), consisting of consciousness (cinmaya), one (eka), endless (ananta), beginningless (anādi).
The act follows: Bhairava-Lord (bhairavanātham), refuge of the helpless (anāthaśaraṇyaṃ), venerated by mind-become-Yours (tvanmayacittatayā), in heart (hṛdi) — vande (I venerate).
Veneration is not ritual offering but mental absorption: the devotee's mind becoming His (tvanmaya).

The name Bhairava performs its own nirukta here: bearing/supporting the universe, the Roar (rava) of AHAM, benefactor of the terrified — all three senses lived in the single act of absorption (Tantrāloka 1.95-100).
Total surrender is sized to its object: the all-pervading consciousness is venerated by absorption into it, not by offering to it.
inference: The Absolute is named in full, then venerated by absorption into it; the name is lived, not glossed. Veneration is not offering but becoming.
uncertainties: Whether 'carācarabhāvaviśeṣa' means particular states or the particularity of states is unresolved.
Whether 'anādi' negates temporal beginning only or all limitation is unresolved.
The nirukta is performed, not stated; the verse does not gloss its own name.
